_comment: Config for scripts/slack_watch.py. Holds NO credentials — the bot token comes from SLACK_BOT_TOKEN or the KeePassXC entry named below, per the same rule as .agents/notifications.json.
_channels_note: Channel IDs the watcher polls for top-level @claude mentions. Start with ONE. #general is C04R93YLPMH; #code-changes (C0BKP7YSQ4W) is a notification surface and should not be a request intake — keep it out of this list.
_claude_app_user_id_note: Every Claude identity in the workspace, so a rendered <@Uxxxx> mention is detected and not just the literal text '@claude'. U0BGZ4YKJF3 is the official Claude app; U0BKALN1A4F is claude2, the bot this watcher authenticates as. BOTH are needed: typing '@claude' autocompletes to whichever Slack ranks first, and the rendered text is an opaque ID — matching only one silently drops half the mentions. Accepts a string or a list; falls back to literal text matching when null.
_keepass_entry_note: KeePassXC entry whose Password field is the xoxb- token. This token is READ-ONLY (channels:history, no chat:write) — the script never posts. Replies are sent by the agent through the Slack MCP connector so they appear as the founder. Env var SLACK_BOT_TOKEN overrides this when set.
_triage_allowed_tools_note: Overrides the allow-list passed to the triage agent. null uses the built-in default in scripts/slack_watch.py: Slack send/read, Xero reads, Gmail reads, Drive reads. Deliberately excludes Bash, Edit/Write, and every send-email tool. Enumerate tool names exactly — wildcards are not verified to match MCP names, and a pattern that silently fails denies the tool with no useful error.
_triage_model_note: Triage is short conversational turns — cheap model on purpose. The expensive chain model is a separate setting below.
_chain_model_note: Model for the handed-off new-feature/fix-bug run. null = whatever the CLI defaults to, which is what an interactive run would use.
_chain_permission_mode_note: The handed-off chain needs Bash (pytest, alembic, git, glab), but its brief comes from chat text anyone in the channel can write — so 'auto' (classifier-gated) rather than 'acceptEdits' (unrestricted shell). It never merges; that boundary is .agents/autonomy.md, not this setting. Valid: acceptEdits, auto, bypassPermissions, manual, dontAsk, plan.
_triage_denied_tools_note: Overrides the deny-list for the triage agent. null uses the built-in default: Bash, Write, Edit, NotebookEdit, Read, Glob, Grep, Task, Agent, WebFetch, WebSearch. This matters because --allowedTools GRANTS rather than restricts — verified: with only the Slack tool allow-listed, Bash still ran. Triage needs no local tools at all, so denying them closes the read-a-secret-then-post-it path.
_agent_timeout_note: Seconds. Higher than a pure triage turn would need because an 'answer' may query Xero or Gmail before replying.
_quota_preflight_ceiling_pct_note: Don't launch a chain if the cached 5h reading is already at/above this. This is the ONLY quota check that can ever block a launch — headless runs have no live percentage to watch (verified: claude -p --output-format json carries no rate_limits field), so everything else is reactive, not preventive.
_quota_cache_max_age_sec_note: A cached reading older than this is treated as absent, never as a reason to hold. The cache only refreshes on an interactive render, so a stale reading proves nothing about the CURRENT window — trusting it to block would silently freeze every request once the founder's terminal has been idle this long.
_quota_fallback_window_sec_note: 5 hours. Used to estimate a reset time when there is no fresh cached reading to go on — e.g. a mid-run quota failure detected by chain_watchdog.py with no recent interactive render to confirm against. A wrong estimate just means one wasted resume attempt (quota_ok_to_launch re-checks before actually relaunching), not a stuck thread.
_quota_max_resume_attempts_note: Caps both flavours of auto-resume (pre-flight hold and mid-run watchdog detection) so a wrong reset estimate can't retry forever at real cost. Exceeding this posts to Slack and marks the thread 'stalled' for a human to re-drive by hand.
